summary.text: Dave Paul is a Democratic member of the Washington House of Representatives for District 10-Position 2, in office since January 14, 2019, and he is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Timothy Hazelo.
A longtime higher-education administrator and instructor at Skagit Valley College, he is vice chair of the House Transportation Committee.

paragraphs.text: Paul grew up in Enumclaw, Washington, where his father was a shop steward and his mother was a para-educator and small business owner.
He graduated from Seattle University, earned a master's degree from Miami University in Ohio and a doctorate from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.

His House Democratic biography says he has taught in higher education for over 25 years, including 18 years at Skagit Valley College, where he is Director of Community Relations, and that he serves on the Island County Economic Development Council and previously served on a local school board in Ohio.
Paul was first elected to the Legislature in 2018, defeating Republican incumbent Dave Hayes.
He serves as vice chair of the House Transportation Committee, according to his official biography.

That biography lists among his legislative work a 2023 law creating a summer Running Start program (HB 1316), a 2024 law capping the cost of epinephrine injectors and inhalers at $35 for a 30-day supply (HB 1979), and a 2022 law helping local governments and ports remove abandoned boats (HB 1700).
